pr_title: drivers: timer: get ppi configuration from dt
pr_body:
Use device tree provided configurations for arm architecture timer
PPIs.

This fixes issue of timer ppi not working on most hardware where
edge-triggered PPI are not supported.

Signed-off-by: Sandeep Tripathy <sandeep.tripathy@broadcom.com>
pr_comments:
@carlocaione   @stephanosio   please review.    Tested on qemu and Broadcom SOC.  Works fine.
First I thought to mark PPI type as level triggered for all.  PPIs are generally level-sensitive configured as per GIC documents.  But I have also seen some dt entries in linux with edge triggered. So better to read from dt.

issue_context.title: driver: timer: arm arch timer PPI configuration to be taken from dt
issue_context.body:
arm architecture timer PPI are connected to GIC distributor interface. Generally most implementation of core support level-sensitive PPI.  Currently the driver has hard-coded
ppi trigger type to 'Rising-Edge' .  

Taking the configurations from dt entry will solve this.

review_comments: This could be in `include/drivers/timer/arm_arch_timer.h` itself, otherwise one has to ensure including `arm_arch_timer.h` before including `timer.h` (via `arch/cpu.h`) - which is ensured currently.

The choice of which type of timer instance to use and its associated routines should be some where other than
`include/drivers/timer/arm_arch_timer.h` .   Currently   `timer.h` seems fine to me .
I see that `timer.h` already includes `drivers/timer/arm_arch_timer.h.` Got confused as both are included in driver file.
